terms.gloss: the water buffalo; classically an African antelope, and in Martial a wild ox
terms.comment: Pliny gives the name to an African beast of the antelope kind and blames the common people for using it of the wild ox (Lewis & Short); Martial already uses it so, in a list of wild oxen. Morgan–Owens takes it for the water buffalo of Asia, with Marco Polo; through the later būfalus it gave English its buffalo. The use for the water buffalo is modern; zoologists call it Bubalus bubalis. The record “buffalo” is the wild ox and the bison.

phrases.latin: Būbalus in lutō volūtātur, ut frīgēscat.
phrases.english: The water buffalo is wallowing in the mud to cool off.
The farmer is ploughing with a water buffalo.

phrases.latin: Vidē, puer in tergō būbalī sedet!
phrases.english: Look, a boy is sitting on the buffalo’s back!

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. bovine: water buffalo.
